coverage.main: Read all 23 pages of arXiv 1906.06919v3 (26 July 2020; NeurIPS 2019 camera-ready stamp): Sections 1-5, Algorithm 1, Figures 1-2, Tables 1-2, references and Appendices A-D (proofs, the averaging alternative, estimation of A, and full L2/L-infinity Tables 3-6).
coverage.supplement: Appendices A-D are embedded in the arXiv PDF and were read. No separate NeurIPS supplement was retrieved.
coverage.excluded_results: Every reported attack (Tables 1-6, Figure 2) is a score-based query attack on the evaluated target (normal or defended) with up to 10,000 queries; the ResNet-152 surrogate supplies only a gradient prior. No zero-query transfer rate from the surrogate to a target is reported. Figure 1(c)-(e) reports cosine similarities between transfer and true gradients, a gradient-alignment diagnostic rather than an attack outcome. Excluded as direct query attacks, consistent with the treatment of direct attacks in other reviews.

f1.evidence: No transferred-example evaluation exists; clean accuracies of targets are not reported for the query attacks either.

f2.evidence: 1,000 random ImageNet validation images are attacked by querying the target; no transfer denominator exists.

f3.evidence: Success is defined for the query attack on the target (within 10,000 queries and the budget); there is no source-to-target transfer step to condition.

f4.evidence: Counts would concern query-attack success, not transfer.

f5.evidence: Numerical L2 (sqrt(0.001 D)) and L-infinity (0.05) budgets are explicit for the query attacks, recorded as positive setup evidence; no transfer result exists to which the field applies.

f6.evidence: A public query-attack implementation exists, but with no original transfer configuration it is neither a transfer recomputability success nor a failure.

artifact_checks.result: GitHub API listing of the paper-linked repository (head 9 September 2023): attack.py, surrogate_model.py, models.py, nets, torch_nets, run_attack.sh. Not cloned or executed; not evaluated as a transfer artifact.

bounds_exclusion.reason: Only query-attack success rates on the attacked target are reported; there is no transferred misclassification rate with a matched clean baseline.

limitations: Classification of transfer-prior query attacks as out of scope follows the amendment's direct-attack exclusion; an independent recoder could reasonably flag this boundary and should see this rationale.
